Triangulated surfaces in three dimensions

Source: R/layers-surface.R
geom_surface_3d.Rd

Grid surfaces estimate vertex normals from height differences along each axis. With shading = "flat" lighting uses the normalised mean of each face's vertex normals and a numeric fill is averaged over each face. With shading = "smooth" the vertex normals are interpolated across each face (Phong 1975) and a fill that varies between vertices, numeric or given as colours such as fill = I(hex), is interpolated in linear light (Gouraud 1971), as MATLAB's lighting gouraud with FaceColor = "interp" and rgl's smooth material. A discrete fill splits the rows into groups, so group = 1 keeps one surface. Binned fill and colour scales split faces at the scalar iso-lines, using linear interpolation of the mapped variable between vertices. Scale transformations place the breaks in the variable's original units. Each piece has one band colour, with normals interpolated across its edges.

Usage

geom_surface_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  stat = StatSurface3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  method = "grid",
  max_edge = Inf,
  shade = TRUE,
  wireframe = FALSE,
  hidden = "hide",
  outline = NULL,
  alpha_mode = "face",
  shading = "flat",
  material = NULL,
  hatch = NULL,
  texture = NULL,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

stat_surface_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  geom = GeomSurface3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  method = "grid",
  max_edge = Inf,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping, data, stat, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard ggplot2 layer arguments.

method

Grid connectivity or Delaunay triangulation.

max_edge

Maximum triangle edge length in transformed x/y units.

shade

Whether to apply lighting.

wireframe

Whether to draw triangle edges.

hidden

Hidden stroke policy.

outline

Feature lines from outline_3d(), or NULL for none.

alpha_mode

How a translucent surface composites. "face" blends every face over what lies behind it, so a surface seen through itself darkens where it folds over. "surface" paints each sheet (a connected set of faces sharing vertices, such as one isosurface level) as one translucent film: other sheets show through it, its own pieces behind its nearer pieces do not. A sheet of several fill colours needs a device with Porter-Duff groups and alpha masks (ragg, cairo_pdf, svg); other devices, pdf() among them, paint it as "face". The raster and hybrid backends keep, per sample, the nearest piece of each sheet and composite the sheets in depth order, with any fill colours; so does the view_3d() viewer. The layers that draw surfaces (stat_isosurface_3d(), stat_parametric_3d(), geom_mesh_3d() and others) accept it too.

shading

"flat" lights and fills each face uniformly; "smooth" interpolates vertex normals and vertex fills across faces. The raster backend and the view_3d() viewer interpolate per sample, perspective correctly. The vector backend draws an isolated triangle whose colour varies along one direction as one linear gradient, with stops that follow the sRGB curve within the option ggplot3d.shading_tolerance (default 2 / 255 in encoded sRGB), and a triangle whose colour stays within that tolerance as one flat polygon. Adjacent smooth triangles and triangles whose colour varies in two directions are drawn as one image per drawing-order run, with per-sample lighting, clipped to the faces' union. The image uses sixteen samples per pixel, at the device resolution and at least options(ggplot3d.smooth_dpi) (default 150) dots per inch. options(ggplot3d.smooth_vector = "subdivide") splits such triangles into flat overlapping pieces instead, at most four times (256 pieces per triangle) and not into pieces narrower than a device pixel, so large faces with distant colours show steps. The layers that draw surfaces (stat_isosurface_3d(), geom_mesh_3d() and others) accept it too.

material

Surface material from material_3d(): ambient, diffuse and specular strengths, shininess, an optional back-side colour and an illustrative style (toon, Gooch, normal colours). NULL reflects ambient and diffuse light fully, with no highlight.

hatch

Hatching from hatch_3d(), or NULL for none.

texture

An image draped over the faces: a texture_3d() object or anything it accepts. Texture coordinates come from the u and v aesthetics when mapped, and otherwise from x and y, spread over the texture's extent (default the range of the layer). stat_parametric_3d() surfaces use their parameters and rgl meshes their texcoords, whose texture file is read when this is NULL. Each face shows the image over its fill; fill = NA shows the image alone. The layers that draw surfaces accept it too.

geom

Geom prototype used to draw the computed triangles.

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

Examples

d <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 6),
                 y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 6))
d$z <- with(d, x^2 + y^2)
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z))
p + geom_surface_3d(fill = "steelblue") + coord_3d()
p + stat_surface_3d() + coord_3d()
p + geom_surface_3d(ggplot2::aes(fill = z), shading = "smooth") + coord_3d()
stripes <- matrix(rep(c("navy", "gold"), each = 4), 1)
p + geom_surface_3d(texture = texture_3d(stripes, interpolate = FALSE)) + coord_3d()
